title: Upstream proxy mode: layer composition and mode selection
answers: How are layers composed in upstream proxy mode?
When does mitmproxy skip sending CONNECT to the upstream proxy?
How does a client CONNECT get tunnelled through the upstream proxy?
body:
- `mode_specs.py:UpstreamMode` parses scheme (http/https) + address via `server_spec.parse`; other schemes -> ValueError.
- `layers/modes.py:HttpUpstreamProxy` is only a marker layer (starts NextLayer). `addons/next_layer.py:NextLayer._setup_explicit_http_proxy` checks `isinstance(context.layers[0], modes.HttpUpstreamProxy)` -> `layers.HttpLayer(context, HTTPMode.upstream)` (else HTTPMode.regular), optionally under ClientTLSLayer.
- `layers/http/__init__.py:HttpLayer._handle_event` on Start in upstream mode: asserts proxy_mode is UpstreamMode, sets `context.server.via = (scheme, address)`.
- `HttpLayer.get_connection` (handles GetHttpConnection) builds `tunnel.LayerStack`: if `event.via` -> `_upstream_proxy.HttpUpstreamProxy.make(context, send_connect)`; if `event.tls` -> ServerTLSLayer (or quic.ServerQuicLayer for UDP), end-to-end to origin; then `HttpClient`. Linked by `tunnel.py:LayerStack.__truediv__`.
- `send_connect = event.tls or self.mode != HTTPMode.upstream`: only plaintext absolute-form request in upstream mode skips CONNECT.
- Client CONNECT: `HttpStream.handle_connect` -> `handle_connect_upstream` sets `child_layer = HttpUpstreamProxy.make(self.context, True)[0]` (first layer only, self.context not forked), then `handle_connect_finish` replies synthetic 200.
